Some ideas below, I think the amount of moderation and number of rules should be kept to a bare minimum. I think the only offense should be when you're trying to use this sub to launch attacks on other users/subs in the way the SRS does. Other than that you should be free to speak your mind. Mods should only act to stop these attacks. Just some ideas though, food for thought.

1. This sub should not be used as a platform for the hindering of a free exchange of ideas.

If we take the charter as guidelines then brigading is a violation of what the sub stands for and should be met with punitive action. Brigading should entail making a post on this sub that encourages users of this sub to mass upvoat/downvoat content on another sub, or actively harasses other users. If you downvoat a lot of someone else's comments, that's not brigading. If you decide to go through someone's comment history and downvoat everything, that's not brigading. If you call someone a faggot that's not brigading. Only when you organize a group to do these things using this sub as a platform are you brigading, and only then should action be taken. What you do outside of this sub should have no impact on your ability to participate in it. That goes for people with different ideologies as well, they should be allowed to speak their mind here. In addition to this advertisements, illegal content, obvious troll posts, and off topic posts should be considered a violation as well.

2. Moderator response to violation of the charter should be well documented, well defined, and completely transparent.

If we accept that violating the charter based on the above should be met with punitive measures, those consequences should be clearly defined and documented, and the appropriate mod action should similarly be clearly defined and documented. I think a three strike system might work. Your first offense results in a day ban. Second offense results in a three day ban. Third offense results in a week ban. I don't think a permanent ban should ever be given out. I think a warning should be the first course of action before each strike. It should be given by the mods and done so in a public manner so that it's clear and the community can decide if it's warranted. You should have a certain amount of time to either edit your post or delete and repost in accordance with the charter.

3. There should be a method for the community to control who moderates the sub.

Lastly I think there needs to be a method in place for the community to vote in or out moderators. A formally styled post should be made explaining who you want in/out and why. Rather than base the results on voats which can be manipulated, it should be based on user posts. Minimums for having your vote count should be set such as minimum account age, minimum CCP, etc. Users post yay/nay, and the other mods count the results and enforce the decision.

3 - i have made numerous arguments about the ability to d-vote and why i think it needs to be abolished entirely, or at least a penalty be paid (in points or something) - here's a copy/paste of one of my arguments...

1) you'll never convince people to comply with what down-voting is supposed to be for and the result is censorship, if not directly, then indirectly because there will be those who will decide to not post out of the fear of losing worthless points

2) the privilege is easily abused by companies that pay people to influence social media or any other group or person with a chip on their shoulder

3) down-voting is at least partially pointless when one has the ability to up-vote

4) down-voting causes unnecessary strife in the community and does nothing to improve the quality of the community

5) as is blatantly clear, it causes endless debate over rules, numbers, CCP, etc., and this will continue regardless of how the existing system is tweaked

6) it is a stick and carrot concept that, in my opinion, has no place in a community that values free speech

considering the above, down-voting is largely pointless in my opinion and should therefore be scrapped, or at the very least some sort of penalty/premium should be exacted when down-voting
